back: A state of complete physical, mental and social well-being, not just the absence of disease.

front: When must hands be washed with soap?
back: After using the toilet and before handling or eating food.
Pathogens in food and water cause cholera, typhoid, dysentery and food poisoning; diarrhoea can kill through dehydration.
Wash hands; cover food from flies; cook meat thoroughly and eat it hot; keep raw meat away from cooked food (also: safe water, clean utensils on a raised rack).

front: Burying waste: one advantage and one disadvantage
back: Advantage: cheap, and covering it keeps away flies and rats. Disadvantage: needs land, plastics do not rot, and it can pollute groundwater.

front: Burning waste: one advantage and one disadvantage
back: Advantage: quickly reduces the volume and kills pathogens. Disadvantage: poisonous fumes from plastics, air pollution and the risk of veld fires.

front: Recycling waste: one advantage and one disadvantage
back: Advantage: saves raw materials and energy and creates income. Disadvantage: waste must be sorted, collected and transported to a buyer.

front: Four routes of disease transmission, with examples
back: Water (cholera), food (typhoid), contact (Ebola), vectors (malaria by mosquitoes; bilharzia by snails).

front: How does a housefly spread disease?
back: It carries bacteria on its feet and mouthparts from faeces and rubbish to uncovered food.
